scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Save the message locally and show it first, then send the request and update the screen as the streamed reply arrives
card.heard: draw a flowchart, tap send to streamed reply on screen
card.say: I'll draw the main path first. The user taps send, and the app saves the message locally and shows it right away. Then it sends the request to the backend, and the reply comes back as a stream. The app updates the screen as each piece arrives.
card.type: draw@chat message flow: flowchart TD ⏎ A[User taps send] --> B[Save message locally] ⏎ B --> C[Show message on screen] ⏎ C --> D[Send request to backend] ⏎ D --> E[Reply streams back] ⏎ E --> F[Update screen as pieces arrive]
card.then: Next, I'd add what happens when the network drops or the stream breaks.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Save the message locally and show it first, then send the request and update the screen as the streamed reply arrives
card.constraints: ["If the network drops halfway through the reply, keep the saved pieces, reconnect and ask for the rest, and show a retry if it fails"]
card.heard: "What happens if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram."
card.say: If the network drops halfway, the reply stops arriving. The app keeps the pieces it already has, so the user still sees a partial answer. Then it reconnects and asks the server for the rest, starting after the last piece it saved. If it can't reconnect, it shows a clear message with a retry button.

card.then: Next, I'd say what the app sends on reconnect, so the server knows where to continue.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Save the message locally and show it first, then send the request and update the screen as the streamed reply arrives
card.constraints: ["If the network drops halfway through the reply, keep the saved pieces, reconnect and ask for the rest, and show a retry if it fails"]
card.heard: "Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it."
card.say: Okay, I'll start a new diagram for login. The app sends the credentials to the server, and the server returns an access token and a refresh token. The app saves both, then uses the access token on later requests. When a request comes back as expired, the app refreshes the token once and retries that request.
card.type: draw@login sequence: sequenceDiagram ⏎ participant App ⏎ participant Server ⏎ App->>Server: Login with credentials ⏎ Server-->>App: Access token + refresh token ⏎ App->>Server: Request with access token ⏎ Server-->>App: 401 token expired ⏎ App->>Server: Refresh with refresh token ⏎ Server-->>App: New access token ⏎ App->>Server: Retry the same request ⏎ Server-->>App: 200 OK
card.then: Next, I'd cover what happens when several requests fail at the same time.
